title: Deck Staining in Archer, FL | Strip, Sand, Re-Stain
description: Deck staining in Archer, FL for sun-baked decks and porches on farmhouses and ranch homes. Strip, sand, board repair, and penetrating stain, back-brushed.
h1: Deck and Porch Staining in Archer, FL
heroIntro: Decks and porch floors on open Archer lots take full sun from morning to evening. We strip what has failed, repair what is soft, and work a penetrating stain into the wood.

questions: How often should a deck be re-stained in Archer, FL?
Should I use transparent or solid stain on my deck?
Can you fix soft boards before staining?

sections.h2: What sun and rain do to an Archer deck
body: A deck off the back of an Archer ranch house or a farmhouse porch floor usually has no shade at all. UV breaks down wood fibers at the surface, which is why unprotected boards turn gray and fuzzy. Then summer storms soak them, they swell, and they dry out hard the next afternoon. Over a few cycles that opens checks and splits, cups board edges, and loosens fasteners.

Film-forming paint on a horizontal surface usually makes this worse, because water gets under it at the cracks and lifts it in sheets. That is why deck staining in Archer, FL uses a penetrating stain that soaks in and moves with the wood.

Whatever is left of the old coating has to come off so the new stain can soak in evenly. We strip failing finishes, wash, and let the wood dry, checking moisture before any stain goes on. Then we sand flat to open the grain and knock down raised fibers and splinters. Soft or split boards are replaced and loose fasteners reset. You can learn what to look for in our article on signs of deck wood rot.
The stain is sprayed and then back-brushed so it works into checks and end grain instead of sitting on top. Railings, stairs, and skirting are done in the same pass.

bullets: Transparent: shows the most grain, needs refreshing soonest in full sun
Semi-transparent: a balance of grain and UV protection; a common choice on open Archer lots
Solid: hides mismatched replacement boards and old stain, with the most UV blocking
body: We show samples on your own boards before deciding, since the same stain reads differently on new pine than on weathered wood.

Porch floors on older farmhouses are sometimes painted rather than stained. If yours is, and the paint is mostly sound, we will usually keep it painted with a floor-rated product rather than strip it all; the crew lead explains the reasoning on site.

Staining needs dry wood and a dry forecast, so the cooler months from October through May are ideal. In summer we start early and pick days with a clear window. If your fence needs the same treatment, add fence staining in Archer to the visit. For product details across both, see deck and fence staining. A deck that is simply dirty or green may just need a careful wash.

faqs.q: How often does an Archer deck need re-staining?
faqs.a: It depends on sun, traffic, and opacity. Full-sun decks with transparent stain need attention soonest; solid stains last longer. We look at the wood at the walkthrough and give an honest read.

faqs.q: Can you stain over the old stain?
faqs.a: Only if it is the same type and still sound. Failing or peeling coatings are stripped first so the new stain can penetrate.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotten deck boards?
faqs.a: Yes. Board replacement and fastener fixes are part of prep and are listed on the estimate.
